Issue Description: Raw pointer used for _libUSBDeviceThread (std::thread*). If the thread creation throws or is followed by another exception path the pointer is deleted only in libUSBClose() but never in the constructor error path leading to a leak.
Suggested Fix: Replace _libUSBDeviceThread raw pointer with std::unique_ptr<std::thread> or std::optional<std::thread> to ensure RAII cleanup on all paths.

Issue Description: In getUSBDescriptorValue(), the loop iterates up to bufStrLen (= descBuf[0]) with step 2. The descriptor header length is 2, so the last valid index is bufStrLen-1. If bufStrLen is odd, the access descBuf[i+1] when i == bufStrLen-1 reads one byte past the valid descriptor data (out-of-bounds read).
Suggested Fix: Add a bounds check: ensure (i + 1) < retValue (the actual received bytes) before accessing descBuf[i+1].

Issue Description: numLanguageIds is computed as (langBuff[0] - 2) / 2 where langBuff[0] is an unsigned byte. If langBuff[0] is 0 or 1 the subtraction wraps to a very large unsigned value before division, producing an absurdly large numLanguageIds and causing the subsequent loop to read far past valid buffer data.
Suggested Fix: Add a guard: if (langBuff[0] < 2) handle error; else pUSBDeviceInfo->numLanguageIds = (langBuff[0] - 2) / 2;

Issue Description: devIndex starts at 2 and increments by 2 per language. There is no bounds check against sizeof(langBuff) (256 bytes) or against retValue from libusb_get_string_descriptor before accessing langBuff[devIndex] and langBuff[devIndex+1]. If the descriptor advertises more languages than fit in langBuff this is an out-of-bounds read.
Suggested Fix: Add a check: if ((devIndex + 1) >= retValue) break; before accessing langBuff[devIndex] and langBuff[devIndex+1].

Suggested Fix: Replace the blocking sleep(2) with an asynchronous retry mechanism or move path discovery to a worker thread.

Issue Description: In Initialize(), if _usbDeviceImpl is null the code calls Deinitialize(service) before returning the error string. Deinitialize calls _service->Unregister and _service->Release setting _service = nullptr. However _service->AddRef() was already called at line 73.
